verses.restored: Having said these things, Jesus went out with his disciples across the winter-flowing Kidron, where there was a garden, into which he and his disciples entered.

familiar.text: When Jesus had spoken these words, he went forth with his disciples over the brook Cedron, where was a garden, into the which he entered, and his disciples.

verses.restored: Judas, the one handing him over, also knew the place, because Jesus often gathered there with his disciples.

familiar.text: And Judas also, which betrayed him, knew the place: for Jesus ofttimes resorted thither with his disciples.

verses.restored: Therefore Judas, taking the cohort and officers from the chief priests and Pharisees, comes there with lanterns, torches, and weapons.

familiar.text: Judas then, having received a band of men and officers from the chief priests and Pharisees, cometh thither with lanterns and torches and weapons.

verses.restored: Jesus therefore, knowing all the things coming upon him, went out and says to them, Whom do you seek?

familiar.text: Jesus therefore, knowing all things that should come upon him, went forth, and said unto them, Whom seek ye?

verses.restored: They answered him, Jesus the Nazarene. He says to them, I am. Judas, the one handing him over, also stood with them.

familiar.text: They answered him, Jesus of Nazareth. Jesus saith unto them, I am he. And Judas also, which betrayed him, stood with them.

verses.restored: When therefore he said to them, I am, they went back and fell to the ground.

familiar.text: As soon then as he had said unto them, I am he, they went backward, and fell to the ground.

verses.restored: Again therefore he questioned them, Whom do you seek? They said, Jesus the Nazarene.

familiar.text: Then asked he them again, Whom seek ye? And they said, Jesus of Nazareth.

verses.restored: Jesus answered, I told you that I am. If therefore you seek me, let these go away,

familiar.text: Jesus answered, I have told you that I am he: if therefore ye seek me, let these go their way:

verses.restored: so that the word he had spoken might be fulfilled: Of those whom you have given me, I lost not one.

familiar.text: That the saying might be fulfilled, which he spake, Of them which thou gavest me have I lost none.

verses.restored: Simon Peter therefore, having a sword, drew it and struck the high priest's servant and cut off his right ear. The servant's name was Malchus.

familiar.text: Then Simon Peter having a sword drew it, and smote the high priest’s servant, and cut off his right ear. The servant’s name was Malchus.

verses.restored: Jesus therefore said to Peter, Put the sword into the sheath. The cup that the Father has given me, shall I not drink it?

familiar.text: Then said Jesus unto Peter, Put up thy sword into the sheath: the cup which my Father hath given me, shall I not drink it?

verses.restored: So the cohort, commander, and officers of the Judeans seized Jesus and bound him.

familiar.text: Then the band and the captain and officers of the Jews took Jesus, and bound him,

verses.restored: They led him first to Annas, for he was father-in-law of Caiaphas, who was high priest that year.

familiar.text: And led him away to Annas first; for he was father in law to Caiaphas, which was the high priest that same year.

verses.restored: Caiaphas was the one who had counseled the Judeans that it was advantageous for one human to die for the people.

familiar.text: Now Caiaphas was he, which gave counsel to the Jews, that it was expedient that one man should die for the people.

verses.restored: Simon Peter was following Jesus, and another disciple. That disciple was known to the high priest and entered with Jesus into the courtyard of the high priest.

familiar.text: And Simon Peter followed Jesus, and so did another disciple: that disciple was known unto the high priest, and went in with Jesus into the palace of the high priest.

verses.restored: But Peter stood at the door outside. The other disciple, the one known to the high priest, went out and spoke to the doorkeeper and brought Peter in.

familiar.text: But Peter stood at the door without. Then went out that other disciple, which was known unto the high priest, and spake unto her that kept the door, and brought in Peter.

verses.restored: The servant girl, the doorkeeper, says to Peter, Are you not also from this human's disciples? He says, I am not.

familiar.text: Then saith the damsel that kept the door unto Peter, Art not thou also one of this man’s disciples? He saith, I am not.

verses.restored: The servants and officers had made a charcoal fire, because it was cold, and were standing and warming themselves. Peter also was with them, standing and warming himself.

familiar.text: And the servants and officers stood there, who had made a fire of coals; for it was cold: and they warmed themselves: and Peter stood with them, and warmed himself.

verses.restored: The high priest therefore questioned Jesus about his disciples and about his teaching.

familiar.text: The high priest then asked Jesus of his disciples, and of his doctrine.

verses.restored: Jesus answered him, I have spoken openly to the world; I always taught in synagogue and in the temple, where all the Judeans come together, and in hiddenness I spoke nothing.

familiar.text: Jesus answered him, I spake openly to the world; I ever taught in the synagogue, and in the temple, whither the Jews always resort; and in secret have I said nothing.

verses.restored: Why do you question me? Question those who have heard what I spoke to them; look, these know what I said.

familiar.text: Why askest thou me? ask them which heard me, what I have said unto them: behold, they know what I said.

verses.restored: When he said these things, one of the officers standing by gave Jesus a strike, saying, Is this how you answer the high priest?

familiar.text: And when he had thus spoken, one of the officers which stood by struck Jesus with the palm of his hand, saying, Answerest thou the high priest so?

verses.restored: Jesus answered him, If I spoke harmfully, bear witness concerning the harm; but if beautifully/well, why do you strike me?

familiar.text: Jesus answered him, If I have spoken evil, bear witness of the evil: but if well, why smitest thou me?

verses.restored: Annas sent him bound to Caiaphas the high priest.

familiar.text: Now Annas had sent him bound unto Caiaphas the high priest.

verses.restored: Simon Peter was standing and warming himself. They said to him, Are you not also from his disciples? He denied and said, I am not.

familiar.text: And Simon Peter stood and warmed himself. They said therefore unto him, Art not thou also one of his disciples? He denied it, and said, I am not.

verses.restored: One of the servants of the high priest, being a relative of the one whose ear Peter cut off, says, Did I not see you in the garden with him?

familiar.text: One of the servants of the high priest, being his kinsman whose ear Peter cut off, saith, Did not I see thee in the garden with him?

verses.restored: Again therefore Peter denied, and immediately a rooster sounded.

familiar.text: Peter then denied again: and immediately the cock crew.

verses.restored: Then they lead Jesus from Caiaphas to the praetorium. It was early. They themselves did not enter the praetorium, so that they might not be defiled but might eat the Passover.

familiar.text: Then led they Jesus from Caiaphas unto the hall of judgment: and it was early; and they themselves went not into the judgment hall, lest they should be defiled; but that they might eat the passover.

verses.restored: Pilate therefore went outside to them and says, What accusation do you bring against this human?

familiar.text: Pilate then went out unto them, and said, What accusation bring ye against this man?

verses.restored: They answered and said to him, If this one were not doing harm, we would not have handed him over to you.

familiar.text: They answered and said unto him, If he were not a malefactor, we would not have delivered him up unto thee.

verses.restored: Pilate therefore said to them, You take him and judge him according to your Law. The Judeans said to him, It is not permitted for us to kill anyone,

familiar.text: Then said Pilate unto them, Take ye him, and judge him according to your law. The Jews therefore said unto him, It is not lawful for us to put any man to death:

verses.restored: so that the word of Jesus might be fulfilled, which he spoke signifying by what kind of death he was about to die.

familiar.text: That the saying of Jesus might be fulfilled, which he spake, signifying what death he should die.

verses.restored: Pilate therefore entered the praetorium again, called Jesus, and said to him, Are you the king of the Judeans?

familiar.text: Then Pilate entered into the judgment hall again, and called Jesus, and said unto him, Art thou the King of the Jews?

verses.restored: Jesus answered, Do you say this from yourself, or did others say it to you about me?

familiar.text: Jesus answered him, Sayest thou this thing of thyself, or did others tell it thee of me?

verses.restored: Pilate answered, Am I Judean? Your own nation and chief priests handed you over to me. What did you do?

familiar.text: Pilate answered, Am I a Jew? Thine own nation and the chief priests have delivered thee unto me: what hast thou done?

verses.restored: Jesus answered, My reign is not from this world. If my reign were from this world, my servants would have struggled so that I might not be handed over. But now my reign is not from here.

familiar.text: Jesus answered, My kingdom is not of this world: if my kingdom were of this world, then would my servants fight, that I should not be delivered to the Jews: but now is my kingdom not from hence.

verses.restored: Pilate therefore said to him, So you are a king? Jesus answered, You say that I am a king. For this I have been born, and for this I have come into the world: to bear witness to the truth. Everyone who is from the truth hears my voice.

familiar.text: Pilate therefore said unto him, Art thou a king then? Jesus answered, Thou sayest that I am a king. To this end was I born, and for this cause came I into the world, that I should bear witness unto the truth. Every one that is of the truth heareth my voice.

verses.restored: Pilate says to him, What is truth? And saying this, he went out again to the Judeans and says to them, I find no cause in him.

familiar.text: Pilate saith unto him, What is truth? And when he had said this, he went out again unto the Jews, and saith unto them, I find in him no fault at all.

verses.restored: But there is a custom for you that I release one to you at the Passover. Do you therefore wish that I release to you the king of the Judeans?

familiar.text: But ye have a custom, that I should release unto you one at the passover: will ye therefore that I release unto you the King of the Jews?

verses.restored: They cried out again, saying, Not this one, but Barabbas. Now Barabbas was a robber/insurrectionist.

familiar.text: Then cried they all again, saying, Not this man, but Barabbas. Now Barabbas was a robber.
